active_ingredients.name: Nebivolol
active_ingredients.class: Beta-1 selective blocker with vasodilatory properties

mechanism_of_action: Nebivolol is a highly selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker with nitric oxide-mediated vasodilatory effects. The d-isomer provides beta-1 blockade while the l-isomer enhances endothelial nitric oxide release, resulting in reduced vascular resistance and improved endothelial function. This dual mechanism provides effective blood pressure reduction with favorable hemodynamic profile.
administration_guidelines: Take with water
Can be taken with or without food
Take at same time each day
Individualized dosing based on response
safety_warnings: Do not stop abruptly - taper gradually to avoid rebound hypertension
May mask symptoms of hypoglycemia in diabetic patients
Avoid in patients with severe bradycardia or heart block
Monitor heart rate and blood pressure regularly
Use with caution in patients with asthma or COPD
contraindications: Second or third degree AV block
pregnancy_safety: Avoid during pregnancy - may cause fetal harm
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.
drug_interactions: Calcium channel blockers (increased AV conduction effects)

mechanism_of_action: Amlodipine is a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that selectively inhibits calcium influx through L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle. This results in arterial vasodilation, reduced peripheral vascular resistance, and decreased myocardial oxygen demand. The drug has minimal negative inotropic effects and selective action on vascular smooth muscle.

Can be taken with or without food
Take at same time each day
Can be used alone or with other antihypertensive agents
safety_warnings: May cause peripheral edema, especially at higher doses
Monitor for chest pain or worsening angina
Avoid abrupt discontinuation
Use with caution in severe aortic stenosis
May cause reflex tachycardia in some patients
pregnancy_safety: Consult physician - use only if benefits outweigh risks
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Atenolol is a cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker that primarily affects the heart. It reduces heart rate, myocardial contractility, and cardiac output through competitive antagonism of beta-1 receptors. The cardioselectivity provides therapeutic effects on cardiac tissue while minimizing effects on bronchial smooth muscle at therapeutic doses. This results in reduced blood pressure and decreased myocardial oxygen demand.

Take at same time each day

May worsen heart failure symptoms
contraindications: Second or third degree heart block
pregnancy_safety: Harmful to fetus - avoid during pregnancy
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Metformin is a biguanide that lowers blood glucose through multiple mechanisms: 1) Decreases hepatic gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, 2) Increases insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues, 3) Reduces intestinal glucose absorption, 4) Enhances glucose uptake and utilization by muscles. Unlike other oral hypoglycemics, it does not cause hypoglycemia when used alone and has beneficial effects on lipid metabolism and weight.

Start with low dose and titrate gradually
Take at regular intervals
Do not crush or chew tablets

Monitor renal function regularly
Temporary discontinuation during iodinated contrast procedures
May cause B12 deficiency with long-term use
Avoid in dehydration or acute illness
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Lisinopril is a long-acting angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor that blocks the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor. It also decreases aldosterone secretion, leading to reduced peripheral vascular resistance, decreased blood volume, and improved cardiac function. Unlike some ACE inhibitors, it does not require hepatic metabolism for activation and is eliminated primarily unchanged by the kidneys.

Can be taken with or without food
Take at same time each day
Monitor blood pressure regularly
safety_warnings: Risk of angioedema - rare but serious
Monitor serum potassium and creatinine
Avoid during pregnancy - teratogenic
May cause dry cough due to bradykinin accumulation
Risk of hypotension, especially in volume-depleted patients
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Prednisone is a synthetic glucocorticoid that exerts anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects by binding to glucocorticoid receptors. It inhibits the production of inflammatory mediators including prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and cytokines. It also suppresses immune responses by reducing lymphocyte proliferation and antibody production. The drug has both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid activity, though glucocorticoid effects predominate at therapeutic doses.

Take with breakfast to minimize morning jitteriness
Do not stop abruptly after long-term use
Taper dose gradually when discontinuing
safety_warnings: Long-term use increases infection risk
May cause osteoporosis with prolonged use
Risk of peptic ulcer disease
May cause glucose intolerance
Mood changes and behavioral disturbances
Growth retardation in children
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Nystatin is a polyene antifungal that binds to ergosterol in fungal cell membranes, forming pores that increase membrane permeability. This leads to leakage of intracellular components and fungal cell death. The drug is minimally absorbed from the GI tract, making it ideal for treating localized fungal infections of the oral cavity, esophagus, and GI tract without significant systemic effects.

Use measuring spoon for accurate dosing
Continue treatment for full course even if symptoms improve
safety_warnings: Do not use for systemic fungal infections
May cause GI upset if swallowed
Discontinue if allergic reactions occur
Maintain good oral hygiene
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature. Do not refrigerate. Keep tightly closed.

mechanism_of_action: Diphenhydramine is a first-generation H1 histamine receptor antagonist that competitively blocks H1 receptors, preventing histamine from binding and producing its effects. It also has significant anticholinergic properties that contribute to its sedative and anti-motion sickness effects. The drug crosses the blood-brain barrier and can cause central nervous system depression.
administration_guidelines: Take with water
May be taken with or without food
Avoid alcohol during treatment
Take 30 minutes before travel for motion sickness
safety_warnings: Causes drowsiness - avoid driving
Avoid in patients with glaucoma or enlarged prostate
May cause anticholinergic effects in elderly
Do not exceed recommended doses
Stop if skin rash develops
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Ibuprofen is a non-selective cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitor that blocks both COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, reducing prostaglandin and thromboxane synthesis. This results in decreased inflammation, pain, and fever. The drug has antipyretic, analgesic, and anti-inflammatory properties. Unlike aspirin, it reversibly inhibits COX enzymes and has minimal antiplatelet effects at therapeutic doses.
administration_guidelines: Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset
Do not crush or chew tablets
Take at regular intervals for pain
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
safety_warnings: Risk of GI bleeding and ulcers
Avoid in patients with peptic ulcer disease
May increase cardiovascular thrombotic events
Risk of renal impairment, especially in dehydrated patients
Avoid during third trimester of pregnancy
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to aspirin or other NSAIDs
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.

mechanism_of_action: Loratadine is a second-generation H1 histamine receptor antagonist that selectively blocks peripheral H1 receptors without significant CNS penetration. This results in effective allergy symptom relief without causing sedation or anticholinergic effects commonly seen with first-generation antihistamines. The drug also has anti-inflammatory properties and can stabilize mast cells.

Can be taken with or without food
Take at same time each day

safety_warnings: May cause mild drowsiness in some patients
Avoid in patients with liver or kidney impairment
Discontinue if allergic reactions occur
May cause dry mouth in some patients
pregnancy_safety: Consult physician - use only if clearly needed
breastfeeding_safety: Generally safe - minimal breast milk transfer
storage_conditions: Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat. Keep in original container.
